const.basis: Pinned per-version wiki records plus documented reference behavior; historical details are explicit bounded reconstructions.
decisions: No arrays in v1-v3; primitive arrays in v4-v6; generic syntax and for-in in v5/v6. Constructors use the reviewed new_* names, with new<type> additionally admitted in v5/v6.
References are always series. Assignment aliases the object; copy creates an independent primitive buffer. UDF may mutate global/parameter array contents but may not rebind globals/parameters.
History stores prior object identities, not deep snapshots. Missing references admit na(x); other operations on them fail. Arrays retain primitive NA elements, except bool NA is unavailable in v6.

Only get/set admit v6 negative indices. For-in evaluates the collection once, reads its current length and current indexed element on every iteration, and binds immutable local targets. V5 resizing behavior is explicitly reconstructed from the documented modern rule.

Statistics ignore NA; empty/all-NA results are NA. Sum/min/max preserve numeric element type; average returns float. Nonzero nth ranks, methods, nested collections, reference comparisons, varip and arrays in request expressions are excluded.

Each run/context owns its heap. Only completed-bar persistent/history roots survive. A private preview copies primitive buffers on first mutation. Checkpoints contain a closed heap and typed IDs; roots and budgets are validated before publication.

Per-array length, total objects/cells/string bytes and per-bar work are bounded. Bulk operations and reclamation consume work and check cancellation. The profile does not reproduce platform wall-clock limits.

const.basis: Pinned per-version reference records and explicit bounded reconstruction; not TradingView execution proof.
decisions: Flat products contain 2..16 resolved scalar results. They are ephemeral return values, not first-class arrays or mutable tuple variables. Each result inherits the strongest dependency qualifier.

Destructuring declares new scalar names atomically after exactly one evaluation; repeated underscore targets discard values. UDF returns and explicit value-if branches share the same representation. Nested products, tuple parameters, tuple reassignment and tuple ternary are excluded.

MACD is recorded in v1..v6; the legacy array spelling is interpreted as a fixed three-result product. BB has no v1..v3 reference and is explicitly reconstructed there from SMA and population standard deviation.

Variance/stdev use a fixed simple-int length 1..100000, last length defined sources, full warmup and exact binary sums/squares. Unbiased singleton yields NA. Optional biased=true is admitted only in v5/v6, matching their reference signatures.

MACD reuses the existing version-specific EMA accumulators: SMA seed before v5, first defined source in v5/v6. On missing source fast/slow hold; the signal still consumes a defined difference. Each written composite call owns one complete checkpoint/rollback state.
BB returns mean, mean+mult*population-stdev and mean-mult*population-stdev. Nonpositive or missing multipliers are not replaced silently.

One unconditional request may return a flat numeric product from the admitted expression subset. All components share one requested evaluation, event, gaps/lookahead mapping and checkpoint. UDF captures, nested/dynamic requests and lower timeframes remain excluded.

const.basis: Economic orders freeze quantity at confirmed creation close, with explicit qty precedence and downward rounding only for derived quantities. This bounded creation-time policy deliberately differs from fill-time equity sizing; gaps change notional, not frozen units. Flat fees are charged on the first actual fill per order ID. Legacy names/early signatures are reconstructed; no external execution equivalence is claimed.
decisions: All six versions have separate evidence. Early signatures and execution decisions are explicit reconstructions.
Explicit qty overrides defaults. Derived cash/percent units floor to the pinned step at confirmed creation close. No future price, close or fill is consulted.

Official equity-at-opening guidance is not claimed as implemented. This profile deliberately freezes creation-time units so pending reservations and OCA have exact quantities; gaps change exposure, not units.
New header defaults to fixed/one. Old headers retain their previous admission and defaults. New settings carry only explicit step/minimum facts; absent limits remain unknown.

Percent fees apply to each fill value, per-contract fees to each actual filled unit, flat per-order fees on the first actual fill of the order ID. Reversal close fill precedes open fill; no future fee redistribution.
Cancelled/unfilled orders cost zero. Replacement gets a new order identity. Only live paid order IDs and cumulative/retired counters survive checkpoint; ledger entry fee residues remain exact.
Only linear quote accounting with pointvalue one. No FX, collateral, margin, leverage enforcement, funding or external execution equivalence.

facts.cash_example: The v5/v6 cash reference example divides the amount by close price.
facts.fees: Fees can be percent of transaction value, cash per unit, or cash per order.
facts.modes: Fixed units, account-currency amount and percentage of equity are distinct sizing modes.
facts.official_equity_timing: The support guide describes available equity when the trade opens.
facts.quantity_override: An explicit non-na qty overrides the default mode and value.

decisions: UTC/24x7 time-based bars only. time is the recorded opening; time_close is the exclusive calendar end, never the next observed opening or a host clock.

Calendar references and single-timestamp functions use UTC. timestamp accepts five/six numeric fields from v2; strict valid dates in the shared calendar range. Missing v1 timestamp and barstate evidence is not silently backfilled.
v2 exposes only documented islast/isrealtime; v3 adds first/history/new/confirmed; lastconfirmedhistory starts v4. Older names ticker/period/is* are separate version-reviewed names.

Historical islast/lastconfirmedhistory use the frozen full input boundary, including research warmup. Observed history requires an explicit pinned historical-end boundary; events after it (or all events without it) are realtime. First observed close without an opening is a confirmed new observation. Recorded mode survives offline replay.

Observed islastconfirmedhistory requires a pinned historical-end boundary; absent boundary yields false. This is a bounded artifact-defined reconstruction rather than exact exchange-open-state emulation.

Instrument numeric/currency/type fields require explicit immutable metadata. Source snapshots bind it transitively through their content ID. Replay configuration binds it directly. No mutable catalogue lookup occurs during execution.

symbol prefix/ticker/root follow the qualified identifier for the supported spot/custom model. No derivative root inference, arbitrary zones/DST, exchange sessions, timenow, synthetic chart types or wall-clock functions.
Requested numeric time/calendar/mintick expressions use the requested environment. barstate and string-returning request expressions remain explicitly outside the request profile.
New programs use closed typed IR .10 and runtime-state .6 with environment identity. Old bundles and old IR structural forms are retained.

const.basis: Pinned per-version wiki records, official documentation and an explicitly bounded execution model.
decisions: No loops in v1. For/break/continue in v2-v6; while in v5-v6. V2-v4 frozen end bounds and the modern direct-var rule are explicit historical reconstructions.

For evaluates initial/end/positive-int step at entry, fixes direction from initial bounds, includes both ends and stops on a missing bound. V6 re-evaluates the end after each completed/continued iteration. Explicit counter writes and collection iteration are excluded.

Statement loops may end with assignments, calls or control. Value loops return their last completed tail; numeric missing is NA, v6 bool missing is false. Flat numeric/bool tuple tails are allowed; string/void values and control-only value tails are excluded.

Each written local var and stateful call chain is shared by iterations. Ordinary declarations initialize each reached iteration. History remains bar-aligned with final variable/expression values; changing a simple TA length through the counter is rejected.
The existing unconditional-global request profile is retained: loops may consume an already scheduled requested value but cannot introduce requests inside their body or requested expression.

All loops in a bar share fixed iteration and operation budgets. Cancellation is checked within execution. Only completed bars can be checkpointed or published; failed/cancelled evaluations are poisoned. No platform wall-clock equivalence is claimed.

sources.finding: For, break and continue were introduced in v2; positive step and automatic direction.
October 2021 introduced while with Pine v5.
V6 evaluates the for end boundary before every iteration; v5 freezes it at entry.
Loop scope, last completed return, nearest break/continue and first iteration of a direct var initializer.

const.basis: Lot accounting is a bounded historical reconstruction: v1 header and v1-v3 close-entry selection gaps are explicit; no external TradingView execution oracle was used.
decisions: Pyramiding is present in v2-v6 local headers; v1 is an explicit reconstruction. close_entries_rule is present in v4-v6; v1-v3 selection is reconstructed.
A positive literal pyramiding or explicit close_entries_rule selects a separate ten-argument declaration. Existing declarations and broker state schemas retain independent readers.

At most 16 same-direction active lots, 16 pending entry IDs, 16 protective brackets and 16 reached commands per bar. Zero pyramiding permits one lot. Capacity is checked when an entry becomes eligible; excess entries are ignored. Aggregate quantity is bounded to 1e24.

Position quantity and average price are derived from active lots. Each lot retains its fill/order identity, original and remaining quantity and cumulative entry fee allocation. Closed slices are persisted in the journal rather than unbounded checkpoint history.

Close quantity is computed from matching entry-ID lots at command time. FIFO freezes oldest open lots globally; ANY freezes oldest matching entry-ID lots. Frozen close targets are clipped to their remaining quantities and never bind future fills.

Protective exits bind current matching lots first, otherwise an exact pending entry order. Pending targets become frozen lot allocations at entry fill, under the selected FIFO/ANY rule. Reservations cannot double-book a lot; reductions do not automatically reallocate to other lots.

An opposite entry closes all old lots then opens its requested new quantity as separate fills. One exit fill charges one rounded fee, allocated cumulatively across closed slices; each lot allocates its original entry fee cumulatively, with the last slice receiving the residue.

Pending entry OHLC order and stop-limit activation deferral are retained. At most one intrabar entry fill per bar; a new intrabar fill activates protection only for the next bar. No path interpolation, observed/live protection, custom OCA or external-equivalence claim.

const.basis: Order groups use a bounded historical reconstruction: v1 signatures and incomplete v2 parameters are explicit; OCA transitions and net-order allocation are artifact-defined policies, not external TradingView equivalence.
decisions: Full local signatures exist in v3-v6; v1 names and incomplete v2 examples require explicit reconstruction.
Net orders add, reduce oldest lots globally, close or cross zero, ignoring entry pyramiding but retaining the 16-lot hard bound. Opposite entry still closes old lots then opens its requested amount.

close_all freezes current unreserved lot IDs in source order, executes next open and never binds future fills. Optional when is named-only in v1-v5; v6 has no when. Immediate fills and alerts are outside this profile.
Explicit OCA entry/order arguments and named protective exits select the new profile. Unnamed brackets keep their internal stop/take peer cancellation. Explicit exit names use reduce.

OCA effects follow actual fills atomically before the next candidate. Cancel removes active peers; reduce subtracts actual filled quantity, floors to quantity step and retains the oldest exact targets. An entry reversal uses both actual fill legs.

A canceled parent cannot resurrect its pending protection. Candidate lists re-resolve current order identity and quantity after each group effect. Stop-limit activation state survives a pure quantity reduction.
One active nonempty name has one group type. At most 16 groups and 32 active members; membership is bounded to current entries and brackets, with no closed-group checkpoint history.

Known open actions retain source sequence, then protections, then at most one actual intrabar entry/net order. Intrabar stop-limit activation and new intrabar protection wait for the next bar. No external-equivalence claim.

const.basis: Partial exits use an explicit bounded historical OHLC model; incomplete v1-v3 quantity signatures are reconstructed and external equivalence is unverified.
decisions: v1/v2 names and v3 close quantity signatures are incomplete; the common named quantity slice is reconstructed explicitly. v3 exit and v4-v6 quantities follow their catalog names. when exists only through v5.
A named qty or qty_percent opts that program into a separate broker. Existing calls without these names retain their legacy signatures. Mixed legacy commands are supported inside an opted-in program.

qty wins over qty_percent. Nonnegative qty, or 0..100 percent of the current exact target quantity, is frozen at command time, floored to quantity_step, clipped to remaining/unreserved quantity; zero is ignored with a reason.

Multiple brackets reserve quantity in command order against an exact pending entry or fill. Modification releases its old reservation. Freed capacity is not redistributed automatically. Manual closes clip remaining reservations in creation order.

Next-open market commands precede protective OHLC checks. All known open crossings execute first; otherwise stop touches precede limit touches globally, with sequence ties. Unknown intrabar order is disclosed as a model, not reconstructed tick data.

Every exit fill creates one closed trade slice. Entry commission is allocated by rounded cumulative closed proportion; the final slice receives the exact residue. Slice gross/net PnL and audit totals are exact Decimal; standard display totals keep money rounding.

Full close/reversal cancels protection of the exact old fill. Commands never attach to a later unrelated entry with the same ID. Pyramiding, limit/stop entries, trailing, custom OCA groups and observed/live protective execution remain outside this release.

const.basis: Pending entries use a bounded historical OHLC model; incomplete v1-v2 signatures are reconstructed and intrabar activation never implies a known tick path.
decisions: v1 has entry names without signatures; v2 has stop examples but incomplete limit/stop-limit shapes. Those gaps are reconstructed explicitly. v3-v6 expose limit and stop; when is admitted only through v5.
A named limit or stop opts the program into persistent entries and the shared partial-exit accounting engine. Both na choose market; other programs preserve their old broker profiles.

Entries are first eligible on the next bar. Limits improve at an eligible open or fill at a touched level without slippage. Stops cross at open or touch at the level with adverse pinned slippage. Quantity is positive, fixed and step-aligned; volume does not split entry fills.

Stop-limit is a two-stage order. Activation at open permits the limit on that bar; activation on an unknown intrabar touch defers the limit to the next bar, even if it could already be marketable. No interpolated tick path or future-price ordering is claimed.

All known open executions use sequence order. Existing and open-activated protection precedes conditional intrabar entries. At most one actual intrabar entry fill is admitted per bar; other eligible entries remain pending with a reason. Protection attached to an intrabar fill first executes next bar.

Same entry ID replaces its exact pending order, resets stop-limit activation and cancels protection attached to the old order. cancel/cancel_all remove pending entries and attached reservations. Missing-target closes are ignored; they do not cancel unfilled entries.

One position, no pyramiding, no expiry, no custom OCA groups, trailing, volume partial fills or observed/live protective execution. Full-close/reversal and partial-exit fees use the separately tested accounting helpers.

const.basis: Trade observations use the existing historical ledger: a closed trade is one allocated closed lot slice, open indices are current surviving entry order, closed indices are stable from zero. Profit and win/loss classification use allocated net P/L, open profit deducts remaining entry fees. These commission and early-version choices are explicit reconstructions, not external execution equivalence.
decisions: Eight aggregate variables have separate evidence for each v1-v6; numeric trade-reader functions are only admitted in v5/v6. Early semantics are reconstructed.
Closed trades are allocated closed lot slices in existing journal order. They are distinct from fills, order IDs, fully closed lots and flat-position episodes.

All profit observations and win/loss classification use net profit after allocated fees. Grossprofit/grossloss partition closed net results. Remaining entry fees belong to openprofit. Exact ledger equity equals initial capital plus closed net profit plus open profit.

Reference wording and example fee subtraction do not uniquely establish every historical commission convention; the net convention is an explicit local model decision and requires separate external validation.
Closed indices remain stable from zero without trimming. Open indices enumerate surviving lots in entry order. Invalid/missing numeric indices return na; no coercion or future data is used.

The immutable output journal is authoritative. A disposable SQLite lookup with bounded cache is rebuilt from its committed prefix, including the unsealed tail. Checkpoints keep only counters and a hash chain and validate against that prefix before broker assignment.

Observations become visible after current-bar broker fills and before primary script evaluation. Requested indicator contexts have no trading state. Historical execution only; no tick-equivalence, margin or FX is claimed.

const.basis: Artifact-defined confirmed history with explicit UTC/24x7 fixed and calendar boundaries; external conformance remains deferred.
decisions: Pine v1/v2 preserve implicit historical lookahead_on, with positional x/y/z/a and gaps=false.
Pine v3/v4 use security(symbol,resolution,expression,gaps,lookahead); v5/v6 use request.security and timeframe. Default gaps/lookahead are off from v3.
Named barmerge constants are required for v5/v6 flags; v3/v4 additionally accept literal bool. Unresolved v5 calc_bars_count defaults are not used.

Unconditional global requests use literal qualified symbol/timeframe. Numeric/bool scalar or flat mixed numeric/bool tuples are computed from bounded pure typed expressions and transitive immutable global bar declarations, frozen inputs, scalar UDFs with private locals/state, conditional values and expression history with literal offsets. Each selected declaration runs once per requested bar in source order. Captured globals with writes or var persistence, collections, loops, strings, nested/dynamic/local requests and trading/output effects are excluded. Max 16 result components, 128 closure nodes, 16 levels; numeric scalar int promotion retains the previous ABI.

Missing numeric values and bool values before v6 are na; missing bool components are false in v6, including gaps_on and before the first visible bar. Tuple components share one availability event. Every requested expression uses the existing typed runtime and the complete frozen input schema/settings; its state belongs to the requested context. No formula is evaluated on the primary bars on behalf of a request. Physical close history for TR/ATR is read in that same requested context.
Aligned minute bars or explicit UTC D/W/M calendars. Weeks open Monday and months use actual calendar lengths. No implicit fetch, resampling or exchange selection. Missing bars remain missing.

Fixed requests preserve exact same/higher multiples. Calendar requests use availability at actual close/open boundaries, including weeks spanning a month boundary; higher calendar rank is D then W then M. Minute primaries must divide a UTC day.
Off makes a requested bar available at its close before the coincident primary close; on intentionally exposes its final historical value at its open before the coincident primary open.

Each written expression has independent state updated on requested bars; gaps_on emits only when a new availability event occurred since the previous primary observation. This gap/event mapping is an explicit artifact-defined model pending external conformance.

const.basis: Static global risk rules v1-v6 use observed open, actual fills and confirmed close. Close-triggered liquidation waits for next open; known-price boundaries liquidate immediately with normal costs. UTC observed days, W/M bar periods and explicit early-version reconstruction; no tick-path or external execution equivalence.
decisions: Global literal declarations activate for the whole evaluated strategy, regardless of source order. Duplicate kinds and dynamic/conditional declarations are rejected.
One composed RiskController reuses the economic lot broker, fees, OCA, reservations and trailing. Old profiles retain exact schemas and observations.
Observe only known open, ledger-updated fills and confirmed close. Never use a future close to evaluate an open/fill risk decision or invent a tick path.

A stop cancels outstanding orders before another candidate. Liquidation at a known open/fill boundary uses that observed price with normal slippage and fees. Close observations defer liquidation to next open, including a period boundary.

Daily limits use observed UTC days; W/M use one chart bar. Consecutive loss days require D or lower candles, use realized profit less all fees, reset on a zero observed day and do not synthesize missing dates.
Each filled order ID counts once per period; reversal and partial exit fills share one count in that period. Only live seen IDs remain in checkpoints alongside retired counts.

Direction and size caps affect entry, including OCA entries, not strategy.order. Entry sizing/minimum admission occurs before the actual-fill risk decision; allowed reductions floor to step and fill minima still apply. Close-only reversal does not open the forbidden direction.

Thresholds are inclusive; zero stops immediately. Percent rules latch permanently on nonpositive equity. Warmup cannot alter risk state. Alert messages are journal metadata, not external transmissions.
No external execution equivalence, exchange sessions, margin, FX or unconfirmed/live risk execution is claimed.

facts.effects: A triggered stop cancels pending orders and closes the position.
facts.entry_scope: Direction and position caps apply to strategy.entry, not strategy.order.
facts.global_stops: Drawdown and consecutive losing days halt trading; intraday rules halt until the next session.
facts.higher_periods: The official intraday descriptions use a chart bar for timeframes higher than daily.
facts.timing: Official risk commands apply independently of placement on ticks and order execution events.

const.basis: Pinned versioned wiki inventory with explicit bounded execution decisions.
decisions: All six versions have independent signatures/evidence. Legacy missing overload details and warmup/NA choices are explicitly reconstructed; named calls start v3.
Lengths and occurrence are simple and fixed per written call and context. Dynamic lengths, string/color valuewhen and nested collections are outside this release.
Events update only when reached, including loop iterations. valuewhen stores true events even when the selected source is NA, preserving int/float/bool type.
Sums, WMA and VWMA use exact bounded-size integer accumulators and finite outputs. Zero volume denominator yields NA; missing source/volume pairs do not advance VWMA.
Momentum uses reached-call history including NA. Rising/falling compare the current value to all previous length defined values after full warmup, not to adjacent differences.
Extremum offsets include NA holes, are nonpositive, use the latest equal candidate, and publish available warmup extrema.
Every kernel has a closed state codec, bounded storage and private changed-cell rollback branches. No wall clock or mutable provider metadata participates.

const.basis: Relative exits and trailing use explicit per-lot historical rules: v1/v2 signatures and early parameter precedence are reconstructed; v5 absolute priority and v6 earliest directional level follow the pinned migration decision. OHLC activation/ratchet timing is a bounded model, not external execution equivalence.
decisions: The pinned wiki supplies full v3-v6 parameter names; v1 has names only and v2 partial examples. Early signatures and precedence are explicitly reconstructed.
Each exact reserved target has its own entry price, effective levels, activation, extreme and stop. Pending targets bind only on their actual parent fill.

v6 selects the first directional level: nearer favorable profit/activation, nearer adverse loss, absolute on ties. v1-v5 absolute priority is explicit; only v5/v6 is established by the additional migration source.

Known open activation and ratchet precede crossings. Intrabar checks use the previous effective stop; a high/low update or intrabar activation becomes effective next bar. No synthetic tick path or retroactive trigger.
Nonnegative whole tick distances and offsets, positive aligned resolved levels. Missing tick metadata and incomplete trailing pairs fail closed.
Unchanged price configuration preserves surviving exact-target state on reissue, including quantity/OCA changes. Changed price configuration resets it. New targets start fresh.
Fixed and active trailing stops choose the more protective level, fixed on ties. Stop wins ambiguous stop/take. Each equal order/role/level/basis batch uses one fill and one fee.
Existing lot reservations, OCA and journal are shared. Effects use actual filled quantities before the next candidate; reductions retain surviving target state.
At most 16 brackets with 16 targets each. Checkpoint contains only current state. Prior broker profiles and state readers remain unchanged.

facts.units: profit, loss and trail_points measure ticks from entry; limit, stop and trail_price are prices.
facts.v5: Absolute parameters override their related relative parameters.
facts.v6: Related absolute and relative levels are both evaluated; the expected first trigger is selected.
